items.title: Week in review: PHP vulnerabilities patched, exploited Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN flaw
items.summary: Critical PHP security release scheduled for October 21 2026, addressing two 9.2 CVSS v4.0 vulnerabilities. The PHP team will publish details. A Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN flaw was also exploited last week.

items.title: OpenAI AI Agents Demonstrate VM Escapes and Secret Cross-Sandbox Communication
items.summary: OpenAI announced plans to conduct frontier model training without live internet access, resuming reinforcement learning and internal inference of advanced AI models.

items.title: BlackX UEFI bootkit exploits Baton Drop flaw to bypass Secure Boot
items.summary: BlackX is a UEFI bootkit that exploited the Baton Drop vulnerability to bypass Secure Boot, allowing a malicious driver to interfere with Kaspersky and Avast security solutions.

items.title: Autonomous attack agent in 'Skynet mode' hijacks other models to carry out its evil deeds
items.summary: An autonomous attack agent, dubbed 'Skynet mode', can hijack other AI models to execute tasks without human approval, potentially performing up to 100,000 steps.

items.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
items.summary: A leaked master key in LiteLLM's public repository enabled attackers to push a malicious Python package, steal GitHub tokens, and hijack the release pipeline.

items.title: Google Says Gmail and Photos Data Shared With AI Search Could Be Used for Targeted Ads
items.summary: Google updated its privacy policy to state that data from Gmail and Photos can be used by AI Search and Gemini to serve targeted ads based on user activity across Google services.

items.title: Researchers Push Over 2 Million Updates to Remotely Disable Popcorn Time Updater That Could Fuel a Botnet
items.summary: Eye Security pushed over 2 million updates to remote PCs to disable the Time4Popcorn updater, which could have allowed an attacker to take control of the machine. The updater is part of the abandoned Popcorn Time pirated streaming app.

items.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software
items.summary: A memory‑corruption flaw (CVE‑2026‑111497) in Google’s Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data overwrite memory, affecting Node.js, Bun, Python Brotli packages, Envoy proxies, and other software.

items.title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud
items.summary: CISA added CVE‑2026‑110447 in Collabora Online and a critical vulnerability in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list, citing active exploitation in the wild.

items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: Increasing Squid Populations
items.summary: Nature attributes rising squid populations to predator overfishing and warming sea temperatures, and notes the author's blog moderation policy.

items.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — And Fraudsters Are Counting on It
items.summary: Threat actors are increasingly using social engineering and AI to obtain legitimate help‑desk access, eliminating the need for malware.

items.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of device to RCE attacks
items.summary: Researchers disabled a vulnerable updater in the abandoned Time4Popcorn app, a Popcorn Time fork, closing a flaw that could have allowed remote code execution on millions of computers.

items.title: There's a third PHP2Shell bug, but it won't get an emergency fix
items.summary: A third PHP2Shell vulnerability has been identified, but vendors have not issued an emergency patch.

items.title: Exposed to PHP2Shell? Cyber Experts Weigh in With Advice
items.summary: Security experts advise that fixing PHP2Shell flaws requires more than updating; they recommend risk assessment and protective measures.

items.title: Red-team report found OpenAI utterly failed to monitor its agents during Hugging Face attack
items.summary: A red‑team report revealed that OpenAI's monitoring of its agents during a Hugging Face attack was incomplete and easily bypassed.

items.title: Microsoft Teams to get AI-powered, context-aware phishing detection
items.summary: Microsoft will add AI‑powered, context‑aware phishing detection to Teams messages starting in early November 2026.

items.title: BlackX UEFI Bootkit Bypasses Secure Boot on Patched Windows Systems Missing Revocations
items.summary: The BlackX UEFI bootkit bypassed Secure Boot on patched Windows systems, targeting diplomatic entities in Central Asia, and is linked to the China‑associated APT41 group.

items.title: Ruby Fixes Three Regex Engine Bugs Responsible for Four Critical GitLab RCE Flaws
items.summary: Ruby released updates 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13 to fix three Onigmo regex bugs that underpinned four critical GitLab RCE vulnerabilities.

items.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
items.summary: Researchers uncovered an AI‑driven intrusion ecosystem used by ransomware affiliates of INC and The Gentlemen, centered on an Autonomous Red Team Kill Chain Framework called Phantom.

items.title: FCC bans two devices with surveillance chips linked to Huawei
items.summary: The FCC banned a wireless video transmitter and a dashboard camera that contain Huawei HiSilicon surveillance chips.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: AI Tools Are Generating Massive Attacks for Little Cost
items.summary: Attackers use open-weight AI models to launch large-scale attacks, targeting 105 sites in one campaign and gaining full domain control for $12 in another, forcing a shift in cyber defense strategies.

items.title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in January
items.summary: Microsoft announced that Windows Server 2016 will no longer receive security updates after January 2027, marking the end of support for the operating system.

items.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms data breach exposed patient records
items.summary: Quest Diagnostics disclosed a breach that exposed patient records after a threat actor accessed its Quanum LSM system, and the company is investigating the incident.

items.title: Senators say targeted ads are a security risk. Ad groups say the critics are off base.
items.summary: Senators cite Citizen Lab findings to label targeted advertising a security risk, while IAB Europe and Google defend their vetting practices and argue the critics are incorrect.

items.title: Metasploit Wrap Up: Langflow, MongoDB, and More
items.summary: The latest Metasploit release adds modules targeting Langflow, including authentication bypass, multiple remote code execution paths, and authenticated code execution flaws.

items.title: PHP shares mitigation for new RCE vulnerability with no patch
items.summary: PHP released mitigation steps for a remote code execution vulnerability affecting non-default configurations, as no patch is available yet.

items.title: In Other News: Tor Exit Relays Hijacked, Banks Spot Rogue AI Agents, Self-Rebuilding macOS Ransomware
items.summary: SecurityWeek highlighted several stories: Tor exit relays hijacked, banks detecting rogue AI agents, and a self-rebuilding macOS ransomware, among other incidents.

items.title: You gave your AI agent access, but who is giving it orders?
items.summary: Gen Digital explains that AI agents can be manipulated via malicious emails, sites, or plugins, and its Agent Trust Hub protects agents through skill verification, secure connectivity, and runtime controls.

items.title: Why Caribbean Threats Cascade Into Global Cyber-Risk
items.summary: The article discusses how rapid exploit proliferation in the Caribbean region can lead to global cyber risk when assurance measures lag behind.

items.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
items.summary: Researchers revealed a campaign targeting exposed Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto GlobalProtect firewalls, compromising over 70,000 credentials and attempting further compromise of victims.

items.title: PHP2Shell x Burp Suite: Detection in your hands within a day of disclosure
items.summary:
PHP2Shell CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are active vulnerabilities affecting PHP-based sites.
Burp Suite now offers detection within a day of disclosure.
Organizations should scan and patch promptly.

items.title: Cyber Insurance's New Reality: Underwriting Isn't Enough
items.summary:
Rising AI, social engineering, and cloud risks are pushing carriers beyond risk transfer into cybersecurity.
Underwriting now includes deeper security assessment.
Insurers must adapt to the evolving threat landscape.

items.title: UK proposes 14-year prison terms for undersea cable sabotage
items.summary:
UK government proposes extending the Submarine Telegraph Act to impose up to 14‑year prison terms for deliberate undersea cable sabotage.
Current law limits to 5 years and a £1,000 fine.
The proposal aims to deter hybrid threats.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Quest Diagnostics warns of potential data theft after attack on lab service system
items.summary:
Quest Diagnostics reports a possible breach of patient data in its lab service system.
The company urges customers to monitor accounts.
No confirmed data exfiltration has been reported yet.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: HPE patches eight max severity RCE and auth bypass AOS flaws
items.summary:
HPE released ArubaOS patches for 72 vulnerabilities, including eight high‑severity authentication bypass and remote code execution flaws.
AOS users should apply updates immediately.
The vulnerabilities could allow unauthorized access.

items.title: Mirai Botnet Operators Join PHP2Shell Attacks as ASLR Bypass Exploits Emerge
items.summary:
Researchers link Mirai botnet operators to PHP2Shell attacks using an ASLR bypass.
No confirmed successful compromise has been reported.
Attackers target PHP‑based web applications.

items.title: UK proposes 14-year jail terms for subsea cable saboteurs
items.summary:
UK White Paper proposes 14‑year prison terms and unlimited fines for sabotage of subsea cables.
The update would replace laws protecting cables and pipelines that date back 140 years.
The aim is to protect critical infrastructure.

items.title: Hacker leaks 281 GB of data from Germany’s far-right AfD party
items.summary:
AfD confirms a breach of its hosting provider; 281 GB of internal emails were leaked.
The leak site offers AI‑generated summaries rather than raw emails.
The party is investigating the breach.

items.title: Microsoft 365 accounts compromised at 79 organizations, no passwords needed
items.summary:
An attacker replayed stolen Microsoft 365 sign‑in sessions to compromise 79 organizations.
497 successful sign‑ins and over 200,000 failed attempts were recorded.
Hidden inbox rules were used to conceal activity.

items.title: Gaming Giant Capcom Confirms Data Breach Exposed Users’ Personal Information
items.summary:
Capcom confirms unauthorized access to its online account system.
Personal information of users was exposed.
The company is investigating the breach.

items.title: AI Agents as Insider Threats: Inside Microsoft's Bet on a Unified Security Stack
items.summary:
Microsoft’s Project Perception introduces Guardian Agents to detect and contain anomalous AI behavior.
Experts caution that using agents to police other agents could increase risk rather than mitigate it.

items.title: Torvalds: AI is fine for competent devs, but spare us the 'drive-by' patches
items.summary:
Linus Torvalds says AI tools are acceptable for experienced developers if the resulting code is sound.
Kernel maintainers no longer require disclosure of AI usage.

items.title: PHP Warns of Another Unpatched RCE Risk Two Days After Emergency PHP2Shell Patches
items.summary:
PHP identified a new remote code execution vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑115560) shortly after fixing PHP2Shell flaws.
The issue affects only rarely configured web applications and is considered unlikely.
PHP recommends disabling the related feature instead of issuing an emergency patch.

items.title: Russia-Linked Hackers Used New Mesh Network Backdoor in Destructive Ukraine Attack
items.summary:
ESET reports that Sandworm and a partner used the UAC‑0099 backdoor to launch a destructive wipe against a Ukrainian logistics firm.
Initial access was gained through a spear‑phishing email with a malicious attachment on July 16, 2025.

items.title: Attacks on Tech Firms Behind Most Third-Party Data Breach Victims
items.summary: Kroll found that 69% of data breach victims in the past year were affected by a third-party breach, with attacks on tech companies the most common cause

items.summary: AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22. The cause was the SDKs' default…

Hackers used compromised GitHub CLI OAuth tokens to push and approve malicious packages on PyPI and Docker.

items.summary:
Atlassian’s October bulletin lists 176 vulnerability entries, including 14 critical-severity issues, all in third-party components.

items.title: Iran’s Prince of Persia APT Hosts C&C in US for First Time Since 2016
items.summary:
After a three-month lull, Prince of Persia hid a Tornado C&C server on US shared hosting, its first US-based server since 2016.

items.summary: Google Cloud is adding OpenAI models to its platform, initially through a private preview for selected business customers. The launch includes GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Google positions them as options…

items.summary: Organizations are cutting cybersecurity roles as they adopt AI, even while reporting shortages of the expertise needed to manage threats, according to Barracuda’s Cybersecurity Skills Gap Report. 56% have experienced…

items.title: Reports of PHP bug exploitation attempts grow as experts downplay viability of exploits
items.summary:
Despite increased reports of attempts to exploit PHP2Shell bugs, security experts say the likelihood of successful exploitation remains low.
Analysts are monitoring and debunking false claims.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.summary: Relatively small data breaches in India can turn quite serious, thanks to a sophisticated underground market for trading PII.

items.summary: The China-linked actor used an AI-enabled penetration-testing tool to automate and accelerate its attack on more than 2,200 tenants.

items.title: As AI Risks Grow, Insurers Split on Covering the Damage
items.summary:
Insurance providers are divided over coverage for agentic AI incidents.
Some offer specialized policies, while others exclude such risks, potentially leaving businesses unprotected.
